parameters.description: The observation reporting the quantified differences or explicit equality between candidate and reference outputs.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning states a tolerance or equivalence requirement for matching the outputs of an independent reference implementation.
The action evaluates both the candidate and the reference on identical inputs within the same check.
The observation reports quantified deviations or explicit equality for the compared quantities, sufficient to judge compliance with the stated tolerance.
exclusion_conditions: The action runs only the candidate implementation, with no reference computation in the same check.
The observation reports only an unquantified pass or fail without comparison to reference outputs.
The comparison uses an absolute expected value rather than an independently computed reference result.
The reference side merely reuses the candidate's own computation path, so agreement is not informative.

accepted_predicates.name: STAGES_CHEAP_PROBE_BEFORE_COSTLY_VALIDATION
accepted_predicates.definition: The reasoning orders verification into two tiers, deciding that a fast reduced-scale check is performed first while the expensive full-scale validation is deferred until after that probe, and the corresponding actions execute the reduced check followed by the complete required workload.

parameters.name: sequencing_reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text expressing the intent to run a quick reduced check before the full or expensive validation.

parameters.name: precursor_check_action
parameters.description: The action executing the reduced or small-scale check.

parameters.name: full_validation_action
parameters.description: The action executing the complete, expensive, required workload after the precursor check.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning expresses the intent to perform a quick or small-scale check before the full or expensive validation.
The precursor action exercises a reduced or small-scale case rather than the complete required workload.
The full validation action exercises the complete required workload and occurs after the precursor action.
exclusion_conditions: Only one of the two verification steps is performed.
The first action already exercises the full workload rather than a reduced case.
The reasoning does not order the checks by cost or scale.
The precursor check and the full validation are not linked as stages of the same verification effort.

accepted_predicates.name: BROADENS_VERIFICATION_BEYOND_REQUIRED_CASES
accepted_predicates.definition: The reasoning identifies input conditions or variations that the stated requirements and given test harness do not exercise, and commits to verifying them in order to reduce the risk of undetected failure.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The agent text naming extra input variations and stating the intention to test them for additional assurance.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning names at least one concrete input variation not exercised by the stated test harness, such as a size edge case, an alternative memory layout, an alternative data type, a malformed input, or an alternative invocation interface.
The reasoning states that these additional checks will be performed to gain assurance beyond the required tests.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning only repeats the tests required by the task specification.
Additional checks are mentioned without identifying any concrete input variation to be exercised.
The extra activity substitutes for required verification rather than extending it, with no additional assurance motive stated.

revised_predicate.name: FORMALIZES_CONSTRAINTS_AS_CHECKABLE_CONDITIONS
revised_predicate.definition: The reasoning converts requirements or preferences stated in prose into explicit, mechanically checkable conditions — such as numeric thresholds, minimum performance factors, size limits, bounds, admissible ranges, or excluded intervals — against which candidate solutions or produced artifacts can be accepted or rejected.

parameters.name: reasoning
parameters.description: The reasoning text that restates the stated requirements as testable acceptance conditions, thresholds, or admissible ranges.

assertion_conditions: The reasoning states at least one explicit acceptance or admissibility condition attributable to the stated requirements, such as a numeric tolerance, a minimum performance factor, a size limit, a bound, or an admissible range.
The condition is precise enough to accept or reject a candidate solution or produced artifact, or to judge its compliance.
exclusion_conditions: The reasoning only repeats the original requirement wording without turning it into a condition that can be evaluated against a candidate solution or artifact.
The reasoning merely lists preferences or observations without deriving any acceptance or admissibility condition.
The reasoning only reports the result of an already executed check rather than stating a condition to be met.
